1. This is a revision petition filed by the revisionist under section 397 read with 401 Cr.PC. for setting-aside the impugned order dated 24.06.2023 (hereinafter referred to as impugned order)
passed by the Court of Ld. MM-06, North-District, Rohini Courts, Delhi (hereinafter referred to as Ld. Trial Court) in Cr Case No.5151/2021, bearing FIR No.230/18 PS Adarsh Nagar in case titled as 'State Vs Ravi Prakash Gupta' whereby the Ld. Trial Court has discharged the respondent/accused Ravi Prakash Gupta for the offences punishable under section 420/409 IPC and U/s 7/10/55 of Essential Commodities Act.

Being aggrieved by the impugned order, the Revisionist has moved the present revision petition on the following grounds :
(i) That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate the fact that accused was owner of the fair pay shop and as per the statement, Sarabjeet kaur, Shri Kunda, Sh. Deepak Kumar, Sh. Bhagwati Prasad and Sh. Praveen Kumar Gupta (System Analyst IT Branch) in the month of March 2018 in relation to 58 NFS Card Holders of FPS LIC State vs Ravi Prakash Gupta on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139779908/

(v) Ld. Trial Court failed to consider the fact that as per statements of witnesses namely Sarabjeet Kaur, Sh. Kundan, Sh.
Deepak Kumar, Sh.Bhagwati Prasad that the distribution machine i.e., e-POS Machine of FPS LIC No.5546 M/s. Inder Mani Ravi Prakash was already seized by Food & Supply Officer 04 after door to door survey report of 58 Card Holders and the same was deposited in Zone Officer and later on the the same was returned to the concerned company by the government.

(vi) Even Ld. Trial Court failed to consider Suspension-cum show-cause notice / order dated 18.08.2018 against the licence of M/s. Inder Mani Ravi Prakash which was ordered by Sh. Desh Raj Singh, Asstt.Com. (North) after door to door survey report of 58 Card Holders and as per statement of witness i.e., Sarabjeet Kaur FPS LIC No.5546 M/s.
Inder Mani Ravi Prakash was cancelled.

It is argued by Ld. Addl PP for state/ Revisionist that revision petition may kindly be allowed and the order dated 24.06.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court may kindly be set-aside.
4.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for Respondent has opposed the contentions made by Ld.

Additional PP for state/revisionist and submits that as nothing was found incriminating against respondent and evidence collected by was not sufficient to form prima facie opinion against the respondent which enabled the Ld. Trial Court to discharge the respondent, therefore, the present revision petition may kindly be dismissed.

5. This Court have given thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of ld.
Counsel for the revisionist/accused as well as Ld. APP for State / Respondent.
This Court has also perused the record.
6. In the present case, Trial Court Record has been summoned and the same has been carefully perused.

Perusal of the Trial Court Record shows that an FIR bearing no.230/2018 was registered under Section 7/10 Essential Commodities Act, 1955 at PS Adarsh Nagar and after completion of investigation, charge-sheet for the offences punishable U/s 420/409 IPC & under Section 7/10 Essential Commodities Act, 1955 was filed against accused Ravi Prakash Gupta on 14.07.2021.

Perusal of the Trial Court Record further Digitally signed by State Vs Ravi Prakash Gupta SUSHIL Page No.4 of 6 SUSHIL KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2024.10.07 17:05:05 +0530 shows that after taking cognizance of the alleged offences, accused was summoned by Ld. Trial Court.

entities.text: State Vs Ravi Prakash Gupta SUSHIL Page No.4 of 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Perusal of Trial Court Record further shows that arguments on the point of charge was heard and vide impugned order dated 24.06.2023, respondent Ravi Prakash Gupta was discharged by Ld. Trial Court for the offences punishable U/s 420/409 IPC & under Section 7/10 Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
7. It is important to mention that at the stage of framing of charge, Court has to see whether or not there is prima facie case against the accused.

In the present case, from perusal of the Trial Court Record, this Court is of view that Ld. Trial Court has rightly discharged respondent Ravi Prakash Gupta and the impugned order dated 24.06.2023 is well reasoned and a detailed order.

Perusal of impugned order dated 24.06.2023, Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that IO did not examine any independent witness i.e. no Ration Card Holder has been examined by IO to verify the case of complainant that as per door to door survey report, Ration Card Holders who were found at the given address did not take the supplies from the accused's shop.

Further, Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that there is no evidence documentary / oral on record to show that variation of food supplies as alleged by prosecution and that the stock register, cash memo and other documents which the complainant was allegedly not maintaining properly were never seized by the IO to show the lapse on the part Digitally signed by SUSHIL State Vs Ravi Prakash Gupta SUSHIL KUMAR Page No.5 of 6 CR No. 323/2023 KUMAR Date:
2024.10.07 17:05:15 +0530 of accused.

8. In view of the above discusssion, this Court is of view that there is no illegality, infirmity or perversity in the impugned order dated 24.06.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court.
Same is accordingly upheld and the present revision petition is hereby dismissed.
9. A copy of this order be given to Revisionist and be also sent to the Ld. Trial Court along with the TCR immediately.
10. Revision file be consigned to Record Room after due compliance.
